title: DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Each local objective f_i is differentiable and convex on ℝᵈ, with L_i-Lipschitz gradient. The public constants satisfy L_i ≥ 0, μ > 0, and nμ ≤ ∑ᵢ L_i.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective is F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ f_i(x), with one local function per computing worker and n ≥ 1. The solution set X* is argmin F.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity.lean, objective and solutions. LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, Params.n, Functions, and objective.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A completed evaluation at worker i returns the query point x and a stochastic gradient g_i(x,ξ) with mean ∇f_i(x). Each worker draws from its own IID stream, and the streams are mutually independent. All parameters are public, including x₀, R, ε, μ, (L_i), σ, ζ, and the timing parameters. The local functions, gradient maps, sampling laws, and witnessing minimizer are instance data.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity.lean, Params, spec.publicInput, and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, Params and system. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.unbiased.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: At that same minimizer z, (1/n)∑ᵢ ‖∇f_i(z)‖² ≤ ζ², with ζ ≥ 0. Since ∇F(z) = 0, this bounds the mean squared deviation of the local gradients from the global gradient at z. Positive ζ permits nonzero local gradients there.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every worker i and query x, E‖g_i(x,ξ) − ∇f_i(x)‖² ≤ σ² with σ ≥ 0. Each gradient map is jointly measurable, and the gradient sample and its squared error are integrable at each x.

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: There exists z ∈ X* within distance R ≥ 0 of x₀, and F(x) − F(z) ≥ (μ/2) dist(x,X*)² for every x. The growth condition applies to the average objective and permits multiple minimizers.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Query points, gradients, and the output belong to ℝᵈ with the Euclidean norm, for public d ∈ ℕ.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, Params.d and Point. LongTails/Setups/DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity.lean, Point and spec.Output.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: A star connects n computing workers to a coordinator with no gradient oracle. Worker i takes h_i > 0 per completed sample and can abort a pending evaluation. A message with k payload bits takes ℓ + b(k + 64) time, with ℓ,b ≥ 0. Each worker has one computation slot and each directed link has one message slot. Distinct links and worker computations can operate concurrently.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, system and spec.valid. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation and communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, clockBits and step.

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: The designated root outputs a measurable point X at the elapsed-time deadline. The error is dist(X,X*)², measured to the entire minimizer set.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity.lean, solutions and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The squared distance must be integrable and satisfy E[dist(X,X*)²] ≤ ε² for public ε > 0. The expectation uses the joint law of the algorithm and oracle seeds. The deadline is fixed by the public parameters, and execution must have finitely many events almost surely through that deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, spec.valid. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents, and TimedConvergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup couples quadratic growth of the average objective and a local-gradient heterogeneity bound at one minimizer with a fixed elapsed-time guarantee on a star. Worker-specific sampling times, concurrent links, message latency, and payload length all enter the cost of reaching the expected squared-distance target.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Minimization with Optimum Heterogeneity

Workers on a star network minimize the average of smooth convex functions on Rd, where d is a nonnegative integer. The average satisfies quadratic growth relative to its minimizer set. At one minimizer near the given starting point, the mean squared norm of the local gradients is bounded. Each worker returns an unbiased stochastic gradient of its own function with bounded variance, using independent samples across workers and evaluations. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is to return a point whose expected squared Euclidean distance to the minimizer set is at most ε2 within an elapsed-time budget.

Let n≥1 be the number of workers, with local objectives fi:Rd→R for i=1,…,n. Define F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x). The optimization problem is minx∈RdF(x). Write S=argminx∈RdF(x) and dist(x,S)=infz∈S∥x−z∥, where ∥⋅∥ is the Euclidean norm.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Local convexity and smoothness). Each fi is convex and differentiable on Rd. For some Li≥0, its gradient satisfies ∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤Li∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd.

Assumption 2 (Quadratic growth and optimum heterogeneity). Let x0∈Rd be the given starting point, let R,ζ≥0, and let 0<μ≤n−1∑i=1nLi. There exists x⋆∈S such that ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,1n∑i=1n∥∇fi(x⋆)∥2≤ζ2. For every x∈Rd, the average objective satisfies F(x)−F(x⋆)≥μ2dist(x,S)2.

Assumption 3 (Local stochastic gradients). Worker i has a jointly measurable map gi:Rd×Ω→Rd, where Ω is a measurable sample space. Its successive completed evaluations use a sequence (ξi,k)k≥1 of independent measurable samples with common probability law νi on Ω. The worker sequences are mutually independent, and the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the full sample array. At the kth completion, a query at x∈Rd returns (x,gi(x,ξi,k)).

For each i and x, under ξ∼νi the vector gi(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and its squared error ∥gi(x,ξ)−∇fi(x)∥2 is integrable. For a common σ≥0, Eξ∼νi[gi(x,ξ)]=∇fi(x),Eξ∼νi[∥gi(x,ξ)−∇fi(x)∥2]≤σ2.

The star has a central communication node and n gradient workers. An evaluation at worker i takes hi>0 units of time. Each worker handles one evaluation at a time, ignores new evaluation requests while busy, and can abort a pending evaluation without consuming a sample. Messages travel only between the center and a worker. A payload of m bits, with m a nonnegative integer, is transmitted with 64 appended zero bits and takes time ℓ+b(m+64), where ℓ≥0 is the latency and b≥0 is the time per bit. The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the transmitted bits. Each directed link carries one message at a time and ignores submissions while occupied. Distinct directed links, including opposite directions on the same edge, can operate concurrently with one another and with worker computations. Nodes may schedule wake-ups and observe time through 64-bit clock readings.

The algorithm receives d, n, the measurable sample space Ω, x0, (Li,hi)i=1n, μ, R, ζ, σ, ε, ℓ, and b. Let T≥0 be the elapsed-time budget and let P be the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the sample array. With P-probability one, the algorithm must process only finitely many events at every deadline t∈[0,T]. At time T, its designated output node must return a measurable point x¯∈Rd with integrable squared distance to S satisfying EP[dist(x¯,S)2]≤ε2.

comparisonHtml:
Each fi is convex and Li-smooth on Rd. The mean F has quadratic growth μ>0 relative to S=arg⁡minF, with nμ≤∑iLi. Some z∈S satisfies ∥x0−z∥≤R and n−1∑i∥∇fi(z)∥2≤ζ2. Jointly measurable unbiased gradients have variance at most σ2, with IID samples per worker and independent streams. On the coordinator star, each worker has one computation slot (hi>0 per call) and each directed link has one message slot (ℓ+bB for B bits). Slots operate concurrently. The target is E[dist(xout,S)2]≤ε2, with ε>0.

source:
import LongTails.Setups.DistributedWeakInterpolation

open MeasureTheory DistributedTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity

structure Params extends DistributedWeakInterpolation.Params where
  ζ : ℝ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := DistributedWeakInterpolation.Point p.toParams
abbrev Functions (p : Params) := DistributedWeakInterpolation.Functions p.toParams
abbrev Samples (p : Params) := DistributedWeakInterpolation.Samples p.toParams

noncomputable def objective (p : Params) := DistributedWeakInterpolation.objective p.toParams

def solutions (p : Params) (f : Functions p) : Set (Point p) :=
  {z | IsMinOn (objective p f) Set.univ z}

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n + 1
  Instance := Functions
  ComputeQuery p := StarNetwork.ComputeQuery (Point p)
  ComputeReply p := StarNetwork.ComputeReply (Point p) (Point p)
  CommReply p := StarNetwork.CommReply p.n
  Output := Point
  publicInput := id
  valid p := DistributedWeakInterpolation.spec.valid p.toParams ∧ 0 ≤ p.ζ
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f i) ∧ (∀ x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
      ∀ x y, ‖gradient (f i) x - gradient (f i) y‖ ≤ p.L i * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ z ∈ solutions p f, ‖p.x0 - z‖ ≤ p.R ∧
      (∑ i, ‖gradient (f i) z‖ ^ 2) ≤ p.n * p.ζ ^ 2 ∧
      ∀ x, p.μ / 2 * Metric.infDist x (solutions p f) ^ 2 ≤ objective p f x - objective p f z) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (ν : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)), O = DistributedWeakInterpolation.system p.toParams g P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (s : Samples p) => s i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (s : Samples p) => s i k)
        (ν i : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
        StochasticSmoothAndConvex.IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (ν i) (f i) (g i) p.σ
  successful p f output P := Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun s => Metric.infDist (output s) (solutions p f) ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
    ∫ s, Metric.infDist (output s) (solutions p f) ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ p.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedOptimumHeterogeneity
